Title: DeepDL drug-likeness scoring
Description: Scores drug-likeness with DeepDL, a SMILES recurrent neural network language model that Lee and colleagues at KAIST trained only on approved drugs, so no set of non-drugs has to be assembled and no arbitrary negative class biases the result. The score is 100 plus the log-likelihood of the molecule under that model, giving a ceiling of 100 and higher values for chemistry resembling marketed drugs. It behaved more consistently than two-class classifiers across diverse test sets, but very short SMILES score spuriously high and the number is not a probability of approval.
Interpretation: Single drug-likeness score topping out at 100, with higher values meaning stronger resemblance to approved drugs.
